prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures a laboratory aisle where the camera wearer walks forward along a long workbench on the left (0.4–3 m away) toward two people in lab coats standing at the bench (shrinking from ~3.5 m in frame 1 to ~0.8–1.2 m in frames 4–5), with background cabinets ~4–5 m behind them and a desk and chair on the far right (~2.5–3 m in frame 1) moving out of view. Across frames 1 to 5, foreground objects on the left counter—dish racks in frames 1–2 and stacked cardboard/white boxes in frame 3—pass within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m) before exiting the left edge, while a hotplate stirrer and red sharps container on the counter come within ~0.8–1.2 m and stay within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) of the two lab workers standing ~0.4 m apart. In frame 5, the camera wearer's own hands appear at the bottom foreground (~0.2–0.3 m away, below the bench), and the nearer person in the foreground partially occludes the second person standing just behind and to their left (~1.2 m away), with both facing left toward the bench rather than toward the camera. The map clarifies the continuous floor-plane gradient, the 3D protrusion of the foreground racks and stacked boxes, and the step in depth between the two overlapping people in frame 5 more clearly than RGB alone. However, it is unreliable in frame 4 where the privacy blur over the nearer person's head causes a glowing white artifact that falsely places their head closer (~0.2 m) than their torso (~0.9 m), and it loses fine structural detail on the distant background cabinets and transparent glassware.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against the unlabelled floor and walls as the camera wearer approaches the left workbench, tracking the primary person in a lab coat from ~3.5 m away in frame 1 to ~0.8 m in frame 5 as they turn from facing away/left to facing left/slightly toward the camera while looking down at their hands. On the left bench, it segments a dish rack as 'sink' in frame 1 (~1.2 m away), two racks as 'chair' in frame 2 (~0.4–0.8 m, within the camera wearer's arm's reach), and the bench surface and equipment as 'dining table' in frames 3–4 (~0.5–1.5 m), along with a red container labelled 'bottle' (~1.5–2 m, within arm's reach of the two people) and a small held object labelled 'cell phone' in frame 3 (~0.3 m in front of the nearer person's chest). To the right and behind the primary person (~3.5–4.5 m away), a cabinet/microwave unit is segmented as 'oven' and 'microwave' in frames 2–5, though in frame 4 the pink 'oven' mask bleeds into the blurred head of the nearer person. In frame 5, the map separates three overlapping people that blend together in the white lab coats of the RGB image: the camera wearer's hands at the bottom edge ('person', ~0.25 m away), the nearer lab worker ('person', ~0.8 m), and the partially occluded second worker standing ~0.4 m behind and to the left ('person', ~1.2 m, facing right/down). The map is unreliable in its semantic class labels (misclassifying lab racks as 'sink'/'chair', the lab bench as 'dining table', and the red bin as 'bottle'), misses the bench entirely in frames 1, 2, and 5, and merges the privacy blur with background cabinetry in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the nearer lab worker from frame 2 (~2 m away) to frame 4 (~0.9 m away) and hand keypoints in frames 3 and 5, while failing to detect anyone in frame 1 (~3.5 m away) when both people face away down the aisle. As the camera wearer moves closer across frames 2 to 4, the yellow torso and limb skeleton shows the nearer person standing to the right of the bench, facing left toward the counter with both elbows bent and forearms raised in front of their chest (~0.2–0.3 m from their body) to hold a small object within arm's reach, and head keypoints angled downward toward their hands rather than looking at the camera wearer. In frame 5, as the camera wearer tilts downward, the yellow body skeleton disappears even though the person's torso is still visible ~0.8 m away, leaving only two clusters of magenta hand keypoints: the lab worker's clasped hands above (~0.7 m away) and the camera wearer's own two hands at the bottom edge (~0.25 m away, within immediate reach). This map makes the exact joint articulation, elbow flexion, and close proximity of the clasped hands across frames 2–5 much easier to read than against the white lab coats in the RGB strip. However, it is unreliable because it completely misses the second person partially occluded behind the first person in all five frames (visible at ~1.2 m in frames 4–5), drops the primary person's lower legs as they exit the bottom frame boundary in frame 4, and loses their entire body skeleton in frame 5 likely due to the heavy facial blur and steep top-down viewing angle.
